summary: Alan Gowans was a scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Toronto in 1946 and at Princeton University in 1948 and 1950, later teaching Michael Willis.

Alan John Bayard Wace studied at Pembroke College, Cambridge, under Robert Alexander Neil. An archaeologist and historian, he held posts at the British School at Athens, the Victoria and Albert Museum, the University of Cambridge, and Alexandria University.

Alan Lomax was an academic who studied at Choate Rosemary Hall, St. Mark's School of Texas, Harvard University (~1931–1932), the University of Texas at Austin (~1933–1936), and Columbia University (~1939–1940).

Alan Sponberg worked in Buddhist studies and sinology, earning his Ph.D. from the University of British Columbia. He held faculty posts at Princeton University (attested 1980–1987) and taught in religious studies at Stanford University (attested 1988).

Alan Watts was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied under Christmas Humphreys and D. T. Suzuki, earning a master's at Seabury-Western. He held posts at Northwestern University, the American Academy of Asian Studies, Harvard, and San Jose State.

Alasdair Urquhart is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh and the University of Pittsburgh. He held posts at the University of Toronto Mississauga from 1973 to 1975 and later became an emeritus professor at the University of Toronto.

Alastair Gornall works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge, became an Assistant Professor at Singapore University of Technology and Design (~2016), and served as a Research Associate at SOAS (attested 2019).

Albert Debrunner was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ferdinand Sommer and Jacob Wackernagel, among others. He held academic posts at the universities of Zurich, Greifswald, Bern, Jena, and Basel.

Albert Grünwedel, a scholar of archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earned his doctorate at the University of Munich under Ernst Kuhn and Ernst Trumpp. He served at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin from 1881 to 1921 and held an honorary professorship at Humboldt University.

Albert Hoefer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Greifswald, Göttingen, and Berlin. He spent his career at the University of Greifswald, serving as a professor from 1847 until his death in 1883, and founded the Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache.
Albert Hofmann studied at the University of Zurich from approximately 1925 to 1929 and subsequently worked at Novartis from around 1929 to 1971.

Albert Lutz is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Zurich (~1975–1986) under Eberhard Fischer and Helmut Brinker, later serving as curator of Chinese art (1982) and director (1998–2019) at Museum Rietberg.

Albert Schweitzer was a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied under Wilhelm Deecke and attended the universities of Strasbourg, Tübingen, and Prague. He held a post at the University of Strasbourg from around 1902 to 1913.

Albert Sechehaye was a linguist who studied at the University of Geneva (~1891–1895) under Ferdinand de Saussure. He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Geneva from approximately 1903 to 1945.

Albert Thumb was a linguist who studied under Karl Brugmann, Hermann Osthoff, and Rudolf Thurneysen, completing his habilitation at Freiburg. He held posts at the University of Freiburg, University of Marburg, and University of Strasbourg.

Albert Venn Dicey studied at King's College School and Balliol College, Oxford. He held academic posts at the University of Oxford beginning in 1882 and at the London School of Economics from around 1896 to 1899.

Albert Welter works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara and Yun-hua Jan, subsequently holding posts at the University of Winnipeg (~1995–2013) and the University of Arizona (from 2013).

Albion Moonlight Butters is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Harvard, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Columbia University, where he completed his PhD under Robert A. F. Thurman alongside numerous other academic and traditional teachers.

Albrecht Hanisch is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn. He served as Acting Director of the Nepal Research Centre and Local Representative for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Albrecht Weber was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin under scholars including Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Christian Lassen. He spent his academic career at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1848 to 1901.
